outcome: The question was answered in the literature well before the window (McClure–Smith 1999, Kontsevich–Soibelman 2000, Kaufmann 2003, Hu–Kriz–Voronov 2003 and others). Since 26 January 2024 the sources record three in-window items on the Hochschild E2 structure: Campos–Hermans (June 2024, prestacks, an analogue), Farr (June 2025, schemes and associative algebras, restated in a July 2026 thesis), and an unread May 2026 talk by Batanin; no AI system is named in any source found.
problem_asks: The frozen Wikipedia wording is: 'Deligne's conjecture on Hochschild cohomology about the operadic structure on Hochschild cochain complex'. Unpacked: (1) Does the Hochschild cochain complex of an associative algebra carry an operadic structure of the kind Deligne proposed in his 1993 letter, namely an action of the chains of the little 2-disks (little 2-cubes) operad, i.e. an E2 or Gerstenhaber-type structure at cochain level and not only on cohomology? (2) Is that cochain-level structure compatible with the classical Gerstenhaber structure on Hochschild cohomology (cup product and Gerstenhaber bracket), since that lifting is what the 1993 letter asks for? (3) The frozen wording names no class of algebra (the wider literature covers A-infinity and dg algebras and linear or monoidal categories) and no ground ring or field (characteristic zero, the integers, or arbitrary characteristic are treated separately in the literature). It does not ask for naturality, canonicity or uniqueness, and I have not added them. Read at its most literal, the item asks for the existence of an operadic (E2-type) structure on the Hochschild cochain complex, with the Gerstenhaber compatibility as the content Deligne's letter points at.

events.what_happened: Getzler and Jones, 'Operads, homotopy algebra and iterated integrals for double loop spaces' (arXiv hep-th/9403055, 70 pages). The abstract, which I opened, does not mention Deligne's question or the Hochschild complex; it describes operad background aimed at specialists. Its place in the conjecture's history comes only from Voronov (math/9908040, 1999), who says his purpose is to 'complete Getzler-Jones' proof of Deligne's Conjecture'. The full text was not read.
events.delivers: Per Voronov's account only: an operadic argument on the Hochschild complex that Voronov describes as needing completion. What the 1994 paper itself establishes is not verified.
events.remains: Whatever Voronov says was missing, which I did not verify.

checked_by.qualification: Working on higher operations on the Hochschild complex; co-author with Gerstenhaber of the higher-operations work
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote in the abstract of math/9908040 that his paper aims to complete the Getzler-Jones proof, which treats the earlier argument as incomplete. This is an assessment of the 1994 argument, not a verification of it.

events.doubts: Voronov's abstract indicates the earlier argument was incomplete. The gap is not described in anything I read.
events.direction: Affirmative in intent: an operadic action on the Hochschild complex is claimed, as characterised by Voronov.

events.what_happened: Tamarkin, 'Another proof of M. Kontsevich formality theorem' (arXiv math/9803025, first posted 8 March 1998; v3 of 13 March 1998 is listed as withdrawn; v4 of 24 September 1998 is current). Also 'Formality of Chain Operad of Small Squares' (arXiv math/9809164, 28 September 1998, 6 pages). Both abstracts, which I opened, concern formality of the chain operad of little squares or discs and Kontsevich's formality theorem. Neither abstract mentions Deligne's conjecture or Hochschild cochains. The Wikipedia article (read through a summarising fetch) lists Tamarkin among the proofs and says some sources treat his as the first real proof. The nLab summary (also via a fetch) says Tamarkin 'proved the conjecture' in 1998. A snippet from a later paper quotes the Tamarkin formality argument as taking the action 'by Deligne's conjecture ([7, 8])' as an input. I did not open the Tamarkin text to confirm which reading the paper takes.
events.revisions: math/9803025: v2 10 Mar 1998; v3 13 Mar 1998 (listed withdrawn); v4 24 Sep 1998 (current). math/9809164: v1 only.
events.delivers: Per the two abstracts: formality of the chain operad of little squares or discs in characteristic zero, and an alternative proof of Kontsevich's formality theorem. The Deligne-specific consequence is not in either abstract. Per secondary sources (Wikipedia, nLab), a proof of Deligne's conjecture for Hochschild cochains. The restrictions are not confirmed from the primary text.
events.remains: If the Deligne consequence is accepted, the classical question is covered. If Tamarkin takes the action as an input, the classical question is not addressed by these papers.

checked_by.qualification: Algebraist working on operads and deformation theory
checked_by.what_they_did: Published an exposition of Tamarkin's proof of Kontsevich's formality theorem (Forum Math. 15(4), 2003; arXiv math/0003052). This is an exposition of the formality argument, not a Deligne verification. I know it only from a search snippet and did not open it.
checked_by.where: arXiv math/0003052 (not opened); Forum Math. 15(4) (2003) per Wikipedia

events.doubts: The withdrawn v3 of math/9803025 (13 March 1998) has no reason given in the listing I read. The Deligne-specific step is absent from both abstracts I read, and secondary sources disagree on whether Tamarkin proves the conjecture or takes it as an input.

withdrawn.what: arXiv math/9803025 v3 is listed as withdrawn; v4 (24 September 1998) is the current version. The reason is not given in the listing I read.

events.direction: Affirmative for the formality result on the little-squares or discs operad. For the Deligne statement, secondary sources say affirmative, but this is not in the abstracts I read, and the text may take the action as an input.

events.what_happened: Voronov, 'Homotopy Gerstenhaber algebras' (arXiv math/9908040, first posted 10 August 1999; 22 pages). The stated aim is to 'complete Getzler-Jones' proof of Deligne's Conjecture'. The abstract describes the B-infinity operad generated by multilinear operations on the Hochschild complex as a quotient of an operad built from compactified configuration spaces of points in the plane. Published in the Conférence Moshé Flato 1999 proceedings (Kluwer, 2000, pp. 307-331), per the arXiv comment. Later versions: v4 20 March 2002; v5 6 April 2016 (current).
events.revisions: v2 12 Aug 1999; v3 24 Aug 1999; v4 20 Mar 2002; v5 6 Apr 2016 (correction to the description of Tamarkin's counterexample per the comment). Changes in v4 and v5 were not read.
events.delivers: Per the abstract: an identification of the B-infinity operad of operations on the Hochschild complex with a quotient of a configuration-space operad, presented as completing the Getzler-Jones proof of Deligne's conjecture. The ground ring or field is not stated in the abstract.
events.remains: Whether the completed argument is complete is not established from the abstract. The paper presents itself as finishing an existing argument, not as an independent proof.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in the proceedings (per the arXiv comment). The referee process was not verified.

events.direction: Affirmative: claims to complete a proof of Deligne's conjecture, with the Hochschild complex acted on by a configuration-space operad.

events.what_happened: McClure and Smith, 'A solution of Deligne's Hochschild cohomology conjecture' (arXiv math/9910126, first posted 24 October 1999; v2 2 February 2001). The abstract, which I opened, says that in 1993 Deligne asked whether the Hochschild cochain complex of an associative ring acts naturally on the singular chains of the little 2-cubes operad, and answers yes. It also shows that the topological Hochschild cohomology spectrum of an associative ring spectrum has an action of an operad equivalent to the little 2-cubes operad. The abstract names no ground ring beyond 'associative ring'.
events.revisions: v2 2 Feb 2001 (current). Content of v2 not read.
events.delivers: Per the abstract: an affirmative answer to Deligne's question for associative rings, namely a natural action of the singular chains of the little 2-cubes operad on the Hochschild cochain complex. Also the ring-spectrum version. The restriction is to associative rings and ring spectra as stated.
events.remains: Nothing in the classical statement, per the abstract. Compatibility with the Gerstenhaber structure on cohomology is not stated in the abstract I read.
events.time_since_posted: About 25 years. No written verification found; later papers cite it.
events.direction: Affirmative: the Hochschild cochain complex of an associative ring has the little-2-cubes action Deligne asked about.

events.what_happened: Kontsevich and Soibelman, 'Deformations of algebras over operads and Deligne's conjecture' (arXiv math/0001151, v1 26 January 2000; v2 27 January 2000 with 'Abstract is modified'; 67 pages). The abstract, which I opened, says the authors develop deformation theory of operads and their algebras using free resolutions, apply it to prove Deligne's conjecture, and describe an operad of geometric origin (distinct from the brace operad) acting on the Hochschild complex. It draws a consequence for the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group. No journal reference was seen on the arXiv page.
events.revisions: v2 27 Jan 2000 (abstract modified). Not otherwise read.
events.delivers: Per the abstract: the Hochschild complex of an associative algebra carries a canonical dg-algebra structure over the chain operad of the little discs, i.e. the Deligne statement, with the restriction to associative algebras as stated in the abstract.
events.remains: Nothing in the classical statement, per the abstract.
events.time_since_posted: About 26 years. No written verification found; later papers cite it, and Kaufmann lists it among the proofs (search snippet).
events.direction: Affirmative: the Hochschild complex of an associative algebra carries the chain-operad action Deligne conjectured.

events.what_happened: McClure and Smith, 'Multivariable cochain operations and little n-cubes' (arXiv math/0106024, v1 4 June 2001; v2 4 March 2002; v3 5 December 2002; 'will appear in J. AMS' per the comment). The abstract, which I opened, constructs a small E-infinity chain operad acting on normalised cochains of a space, with a suboperad quasi-isomorphic to the chains of the little n-cubes operad. For n = 2 it says this 'leads to a substantial simplification of our earlier proof of Deligne's Hochschild cohomology conjecture'.
events.delivers: Per the abstract, a simplified proof of the same little-2-cubes action as the 1999 paper. The ground ring is not stated on the abstract page.
events.remains: Nothing beyond the 1999 event, since it is the same question.

checked_by.who: Journal of the American Mathematical Society (per the arXiv comment)
checked_by.what_they_did: Stated as forthcoming in J. AMS at the time of the arXiv record. Acceptance and publication were not confirmed.

events.what_happened: Berger and Fresse, 'Combinatorial operad actions on cochains' (arXiv math/0109158, first posted 21 September 2001; v2 21 October 2002; Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 137 (2004), 135-174, per the arXiv record). The abstract, which I opened, says the Barratt-Eccles operad acts on the normalised cochains of a simplicial set, and that for the normalised Hochschild cochain complex of an associative algebra a suboperad acts and is 'equivalent to the classical little squares operad'. The abstract does not mention Deligne's conjecture; the link is drawn in later sources (search snippets).
events.delivers: Per the abstract: a suboperad of the Barratt-Eccles operad acts on the normalised Hochschild cochain complex of an associative algebra and is equivalent to the little squares operad. This is the Deligne-type action; the ground ring or field is not stated.
events.remains: Nothing in the classical statement, per the abstract, subject to the unstated ring.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2004 (per the arXiv journal reference). The referee process was not seen.

events.direction: Affirmative for the Hochschild action of a little-squares suboperad; the Deligne link is drawn by secondary sources, not the abstract.

events.what_happened: Kaufmann, 'On Spineless Cacti, Deligne's Conjecture and Connes-Kreimer's Hopf Algebra' (arXiv math/0308005, first posted 1 August 2003; v4 25 October 2006; 'Version to appear in Topology'). The abstract, which I opened, says cellular chains of normalised spineless cacti give a model of the little discs operad, and that this gives 'a solution to Deligne's conjecture on the Hochschild complex', together with the Connes-Kreimer Hopf algebra and Chas-Sullivan string topology. A search snippet describes it as a new direct proof. The ground field is not stated on the abstract page.
events.revisions: v2 21 Mar 2004; v3 10 Feb 2006; v4 25 Oct 2006 (version shown on the arXiv page).
events.delivers: Per the abstract, a cactus-based proof of the Hochschild E2 action, described as a solution of Deligne's conjecture on the Hochschild complex. The ground ring is not stated in the abstract.
events.remains: Nothing in the classical statement, per the abstract.

checked_by.what_they_did: The arXiv comment states the version is to appear in Topology. Acceptance and publication were not confirmed.

events.direction: Affirmative: a direct cactus-based proof of the Hochschild E2 action.

events.what_happened: Hu, Kriz and Voronov, 'On Kontsevich's Hochschild cohomology conjecture' (arXiv math/0309369, first posted 22 September 2003; v2 7 January 2005; 'final version, to appear in Compos. Math.'). The abstract, which I opened, proves that for an E_n-algebra (an algebra over the chains of the little n-cubes operad) the Hochschild cohomology complex is an E_{n+1}-algebra. It says the n = 1 case 'generalizes a conjecture by Deligne', and that Deligne's case has been proven by several authors.
events.delivers: A general E_n to E_{n+1} result. Per the abstract it covers the n = 1 case, the Deligne E2 structure on Hochschild cochains, as a special case. The ground ring is not stated in the abstract.
events.remains: Nothing in the classical statement, per the abstract.

checked_by.what_they_did: The arXiv comment says the version is to appear in Compos. Math. A later reference gives Compositio 142 (2006), 143-168 (search snippet). The referee process was not seen.

events.direction: Affirmative: the E_n to E_{n+1} result includes Deligne's case n = 1.

events.what_happened: Lurie, 'Derived Algebraic Geometry VI: E_k Algebras' (arXiv 0911.0018, first posted 30 October 2009; 226 pages; single version). The abstract, which I opened, describes E_k-algebras in higher category theory and says nothing about Deligne. Secondary sources (nLab, and Farr 2025 as summarised) cite it as the general argument that E_k-centres in symmetric monoidal (infinity,1)-categories give E_{k+1}-structures, which covers the Deligne case. I did not locate that statement in the text, which I could not read beyond the abstract.
events.delivers: Per secondary sources only: a general E_k-centre construction giving E_{k+1}-structures in symmetric monoidal (infinity,1)-categories, which covers Hochschild cochains. Not verified against the primary text.
events.remains: Not established from what I read.
events.time_since_posted: About 17 years. Widely cited as the general framework; no referee record found; text not read.
events.direction: Affirmative in general, per secondary sources.

events.what_happened: Zhengfang Wang, 'Gerstenhaber algebra and Deligne's conjecture on Tate-Hochschild cohomology' (arXiv 1801.07990, first posted 24 January 2018; single version; 47 pages). The abstract, which I opened, builds a 'singular Hochschild cochain complex' for any associative algebra over a field, using non-commutative differential forms. Using Kaufmann's spineless cacti action, it proves Deligne's conjecture for that complex. For self-injective algebras the Tate-Hochschild cohomology is recovered, and for symmetric algebras it is a BV algebra.
events.delivers: Per the abstract: a Deligne-type E2 action on a different complex, the singular Hochschild cochain complex, which is quasi-isomorphic to Tate-Hochschild cohomology only in the self-injective case. It does not address the ordinary Hochschild cochain complex of an associative algebra in general.
events.remains: The ordinary Hochschild cochain complex statement, per the abstract.
events.time_since_posted: About 8 years. No written verification found.
events.direction: Affirmative for a different complex (a variant of the Hochschild cochain complex).

events.what_happened: Batanin and Davydov, 'Cosimplicial monoids and deformation theory of tensor categories' (arXiv 2003.13039, first posted 29 March 2020; v2 16 January 2023; J. Noncommut. Geom. 17 (2023), 1167-1229, per a search snippet). The abstract, which I opened, gives E_{n+1}-algebra structures on total objects of n-commutative cosimplicial monoids. The deformation complex of a tensor functor is E_2, and that of a tensor category is E_3. The abstract presents the E_2 claim as parallel to the Hochschild case, not as a proof of Deligne's conjecture.
events.delivers: An E_2-structure on the deformation complex of a tensor functor, and E_3 for tensor categories. These are different objects from the Hochschild cochain complex of an associative algebra.
events.remains: The whole Hochschild question, which is not addressed.

checked_by.who: Journal of Noncommutative Geometry (per a search snippet, not verified on the journal page)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published as J. Noncommut. Geom. 17 (2023). Referee process not seen.

events.direction: Analogue: an E_2-structure on a different object (deformation complex of a tensor functor). Affirmative for that object.

events.what_happened: Brav and Rozenblyum, 'The cyclic Deligne conjecture and Calabi-Yau structures' (arXiv 2305.10323, first posted 17 May 2023; one version listed; math.AT). The HTML text, which I read in its first 100,000 characters, has Theorem 1.0.1: for a dualizable linear category with a Calabi-Yau structure (smooth or proper), the Hochschild cochains carry a framed E2-structure refining the E2-structure 'provided by the solution of the Deligne conjecture'. Application: chain-level genus-zero string topology operations on relative loop homology. The acknowledgements thank Damien Calaque, David Ayala, Dmitry Kaledin, Manuel Rivera and Mahmoud Zeinalian, and give a Basis Foundation grant. No AI or software disclosure. Talks on the work followed (Tsinghua and BIMSA, Nov 2024; CMS Winter 2025), but these are talks, not separate events.
events.revisions: v1 only on the arXiv record I read.
events.delivers: A cyclic (framed E2) refinement of the Hochschild E2 structure under a Calabi-Yau hypothesis on the linear category. It takes the non-cyclic Deligne E2 structure as given, per the theorem's phrasing.
events.remains: The non-cyclic classical statement, which the paper uses rather than re-proves.
events.time_since_posted: About 3 years 5 months. No journal publication found in searches; no written verification found.
events.direction: Affirmative for the cyclic refinement under a Calabi-Yau hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Aguilar Martín and Roitzheim, 'The Derived Deligne Conjecture' (arXiv 2307.11414, first posted 21 July 2023; v2 2 August 2023; v3 23 September 2024). The abstract, which I read through a summarising fetch, develops a brace-algebra framework on operads for derived A-infinity-algebras, generalising the Lie structure on the Hochschild complex of an A-infinity-algebra, and says it yields 'new and rigorous versions of the Deligne conjecture'. The v3 revision of 23 September 2024 falls in the window; I did not read what it changed.
events.revisions: v2 2 Aug 2023; v3 23 Sep 2024 (inside the window; content not read).
events.delivers: Per the abstract: versions of the Deligne-type statement for derived A-infinity-algebras, a different algebraic input from associative algebras. The exact statements were not read.
events.remains: Whether the statement for associative algebras is covered is not established from the abstract.
events.time_since_posted: About 3 years 2 months from v1. No written verification found.
events.direction: Analogue: derived A-infinity-algebras. Affirmative for those versions.

events.what_happened: Talk by Jiahao Cheng (程家豪, Nanchang Hangkong University; joint work with Z. Chen, Y. Qiao and M. Xiang) at the USTC algebra seminar on 29 November 2023, titled 'Deligne's conjecture for Lie algebroid pairs' per a search snippet. It claims a homotopy braces algebra from a Lie algebroid pair, and that the Hochschild cochain complex of a Lie algebroid pair is an algebra over the little 2-discs operad. I found no preprint in searches. I know this only from the seminar listing snippet; I did not open the page.

events.remains: Everything beyond the talk abstract, since no paper was found.
events.time_since_posted: Talk only; no preprint located in searches.
events.direction: Analogue: an E_2-structure on Hochschild cochains of Lie algebroid pairs. Affirmative for that analogue.

events.what_happened: Campos and Hermans, 'A Deligne conjecture for prestacks' (arXiv 2406.16652, first posted 24 June 2024, inside the window; v2 13 March 2025; 'To appear in Proceedings of the AMS'). The abstract and HTML, which I read in its first 100,000 characters, say that for a prestack the Gerstenhaber-Schack complex is naturally an E2-algebra (Theorem 1.6: an action of the E2-operad TwQuilt). It recovers the known L-infinity and Gerstenhaber structures and proves Hawkins's conjecture that the dg operad Quilt has vanishing positive-degree homology, so Quilt is quasi-isomorphic to Brace. Published Proc. AMS 153 (2025), no. 10, 4155-4175, DOI 10.1090/proc/17293, per search results; the AMS page returned HTTP 403.
events.revisions: v2 13 Mar 2025; published Proc. AMS, Oct 2025 (per search results).
events.delivers: An E2-structure on the Gerstenhaber-Schack complex of a prestack, with the restriction to prestacks as stated in the abstract. It does not address Hochschild cochains of associative algebras, and the paper's own account does not claim to.
events.remains: The classical statement for the Hochschild cochain complex of an associative algebra, which this paper does not touch on its own account.

events.what_happened: Farr, 'E2-algebra structures on the derived center of an algebraic scheme' (arXiv 2506.14069, v1 submitted 16 June 2025, inside the window; single version; 55 pages; math.AT, math.AG, math.QA). The abstract, read through a fetch paraphrase, says that via Lurie's higher centres and an infinity-operadic centre, the Hochschild complex of a k-scheme carries a canonical E2-structure. It says this 'recovers a canonical solution to Deligne's conjecture' in the affine and global cases, including singular schemes, and that the structure agrees with the Gerstenhaber bracket and cup product in the affine and smooth cases. The HTML (first 100,000 of 108,958 characters, read through a fetch summary) gives Theorem A: for an associative k-algebra A, the Hochschild complex with the evaluation map is an E1-centre of A in Alg_E1(D-infinity(k)), hence E2. For schemes, the Hochschild cochain complex is defined as the centre of the structure sheaf in dg sheaves; Theorem B recovers the affine centre on affine opens. Acknowledgements thank Nick Rozenblyum for 'invaluable comments on J. Lurie's proof of the Dunn Additivity Theorem' and Dennis Borisov for discussions; funding NSF DMS-2305407. No AI or software disclosure in the part read.
events.revisions: None found: arXiv lists v1 only.
events.delivers: Per Theorem A (as summarised): an E2-structure on the Hochschild cochain complex of any associative k-algebra, realised as a centre, with the Gerstenhaber bracket and cup product agreeing on cohomology in the affine smooth case (abstract). Per the abstract: a global version for k-schemes, including singular ones, defined through the centre of the structure sheaf. Restrictions: the global and singular statements concern schemes and a scheme-level definition of Hochschild cochains; the field k is general in the text as read, and characteristic is not discussed in what I read.
events.remains: Per the abstract, the agreement is claimed at the level of the Gerstenhaber bracket and cup product on cohomology. Whether the cochain-level E2 structure coincides with the earlier McClure-Smith and Kontsevich-Soibelman actions is not stated in the abstract or the parts read. The cyclic or framed version is not claimed.
events.time_since_posted: About 16 months to 10 October 2026. No outside verification or citing paper found in searches (a citation-graph search was not run). Acknowledged comments by Nick Rozenblyum on one ingredient are not recorded as a verification.
events.direction: Affirmative: asserts a canonical E2-structure on Hochschild cochains. For associative algebras this is Theorem A in the affine case, and for k-schemes (including singular ones) it is the global and singular extension.

events.what_happened: Farr, 'Derived operadic centers in algebraic geometry and deformation quantization' (arXiv 2607.05455, v1 submitted 5 July 2026, inside the window; single version; 112 pages; comment 'Comments welcome'). The arXiv abstract, read through a fetch paraphrase, restates the 2025 main result: a canonical solution to Deligne's conjecture for Hochschild cochains, in affine and global settings including singular schemes, via an infinity-operadic centre, agreeing with the Gerstenhaber bracket and cup product in the affine and smooth cases. It adds links to operadic formal moduli problems and formal automorphism groups, and is motivated by the square root of the Todd genus in Kontsevich's formality theorem. The HTML (first 100,000 of 178,304 characters) says: 'This is the author's Ph.D. thesis, submitted to the University of Nevada, Reno, in August 2026.' That date is later than the arXiv v1 date and is not reconciled in the text. Theorem 4.2.20 and Corollary 4.2.23 give the affine statement ('together with the evaluation map is a center for A'). Acknowledgements thank the advisor Christopher Rogers, Marc Levine and Damien Calaque, and give NSF DMS-2305407. No AI or software disclosure in the part read.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv (5 Jul 2026). The thesis text dates its submission to August 2026, which does not match the arXiv date.
events.delivers: Restates the 2025 result: a canonical E2-structure on Hochschild cochains, affine (for associative algebras) and global, including singular schemes. The abstract adds material on formal moduli problems and formal automorphisms; the new content relative to the 2025 paper was not identified in what I read.
events.remains: As for the 2025 event: the cochain-level comparison with the earlier actions is not stated in the parts read.
events.time_since_posted: About 3 months to 10 October 2026. No outside verification found. Whether a doctoral committee approved the thesis is not shown in the text read.
events.direction: Affirmative: the same canonical E2-structure claim as the 2025 event.

disputes.summary: Whether Tamarkin's 1998 work proves Deligne's conjecture or takes it as an input. Wikipedia (via a fetch summary) and nLab (via a fetch summary) list Tamarkin among the proofs, and Wikipedia says some sources treat his as the first real proof. The abstracts of math/9803025 and math/9809164, which I read, do not mention Deligne. A later paper's snippet quotes the formality argument as taking the action 'by Deligne's conjecture' as an input. Recorded both ways; not resolved here.

Getzler and Jones (1994) are named as the first attempt; Voronov (1999) says his paper completes the Getzler-Jones proof. Whether the 1994 argument was a complete proof is not established, since I did not read the 1994 text.

A search snippet reports that McClure and Smith describe their results as found independently, with a different choice of signs, in joint work of Berger and Fresse. Not verified in the primary text; recorded as reported.

Farr (2025 and 2026) describes the affine and global E2-structure as a 'canonical solution' or as 'recovering' a solution to Deligne's conjecture. The classical solutions for associative algebras date from 1999 to 2003. Whether the Farr papers are a new solution or a new canonical construction of an already-solved statement is for the judging pass.

summary: The Hochschild E2 question has been answered in the literature since 1999. The primary sources I read give McClure and Smith (math/9910126, Oct 1999; simplified math/0106024, June 2001), Kontsevich and Soibelman (math/0001151, Jan 2000), Berger and Fresse (math/0109158, Sept 2001, a little-squares action on normalised Hochschild cochains, with the Deligne link drawn elsewhere), Kaufmann (math/0308005, Aug 2003, cactus proof) and Hu, Kriz and Voronov (math/0309369, Sept 2003, E_n to E_{n+1}, covering n = 1). Earlier attempts are Getzler and Jones (1994, which Voronov says needed completing) and Tamarkin (1998), whose role in the Deligne statement is disputed (see disputes). Later pre-window work covers variants: Wang 2018 (singular Hochschild complex), Batanin and Davydov 2020 (tensor functors), Brav and Rozenblyum 2023 (cyclic version under Calabi-Yau), Aguilar Martín and Roitzheim 2023 (derived A-infinity, revised Sept 2024) and a 2023 Lie-algebroid talk with no preprint found. The Wikipedia article (read through a summarising fetch, so the lead is not verified verbatim) says the statement section needs expansion, that it needs an expert in mathematics, and that it was last edited on 11 July 2026. In the window, three events are recorded. Campos and Hermans (arXiv 24 June 2024, Proc. AMS 2025) give an E2-structure on the Gerstenhaber-Schack complex of a prestack, an analogue that does not address Hochschild cochains of associative algebras. Farr (arXiv 16 June 2025) gives, in Theorem A, an E2-structure on the Hochschild cochain complex of an associative k-algebra, realised as an E1-centre, and in the global and singular cases a structure on schemes. Farr's thesis (arXiv 5 July 2026) restates the same claim. The thesis HTML says it was submitted in August 2026, which does not match the arXiv date and is not reconciled. A May 2026 Batanin talk is recorded from a snippet; its slides could not be read. No independent verification, citing paper or refereed publication of the Farr work was found, and the Campos-Hermans paper's referee reports were not seen. The close call is whether the Farr papers move the item. Farr's abstract says 'recovers', so the classical statement appears to be re-derived rather than newly settled, but Theorem A's affine case is stated for arbitrary associative algebras, which is the item's own setting. No AI system is named in any source I read, and searches for AI involvement on this item (including AI trackers, the Erdős and FrontierMath trackers, AlphaEvolve, AxiomProver and Aristotle) returned nothing on it. No Lean or Coq formalisation was found.
competing_reading: Read the Farr papers (June 2025; July 2026) as a resolution-type event. Theorem A gives an E2-structure on the Hochschild cochain complex of any associative algebra, which is the item's own setting ('operadic structure on Hochschild cochain complex'), and the global and singular claims extend it to schemes. On this reading the item moved in the window, through a canonical construction that is new in its method. The opposing reading: the item asks the classical question, which McClure-Smith, Kontsevich-Soibelman, Kaufmann and Hu-Kriz-Voronov answered between 1999 and 2003. Farr's own abstract says 'recovers', and the new content is a canonical construction via higher centres and a scheme-level definition, not a new answer. On this reading nothing in the window moved the item, and the in-window papers are a re-derivation (Farr) and an analogue (Campos-Hermans).
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of Farr 2025 and 2026 past the first 100,000 characters I read: the exact statement of Theorem A, the ground ring, whether the E2-structure it produces is the one McClure-Smith and Kontsevich-Soibelman describe, and whether it is compatible with cup product and bracket at cochain level. (2) Any written verification of Farr 2025 by an expert, or a citing paper that addresses it; none was found, and a citation-graph search was not run. (3) The content of the May 2026 Batanin slides, which were unreadable through the fetch tool. (4) The Wikipedia article's statement section and talk page, to see which precise claim the list bullet points to, and whether it asks for naturality or canonicity beyond existence. (5) Whether the Lie-algebroid preprint exists and, if it appeared in 2024 or later, what it establishes. (6) The Hess review of the history, which failed to load.
